transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-09
Start: 16:42 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Reddy (Nebula Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Nebula SRE), Sara Park (Nebula Security), Tom Alvarez (Nebula Product)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, and request-logs for debugging production inference issues. Customer is evaluating dedicated vs hosted for latency-sensitive payment flows; strong security requirements (SAML/SSO, KMS, audit logs). Agreed to run an initial POC with sample traffic.

Topics: tracing UI, request-logs, error-analysis, correlating traces with request-ids, retention policy, RBAC, network/VPC options, POC scope and next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: alright everyone can hear me? good afternoon, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, this is priya and liam from our solutions team.
[00:08] Maya: yeah we can hear you, thanks, the time works — appreciate it.
[00:12] Jordan: great, quick agenda — we'll show the console tracing flows, how we correlate request-logs to traces for error analysis, then hands-on demo on a failing request and the debugging flow. finally we'll cover security and next steps. sound good?
[00:26] Ethan: yep that's perfect, we're mostly concerned about two things: preventing flaky inference responses in payment flows and being able to triage latency spikes.
[00:35] Priya: cool, that's exactly the scenario we'll walk through. i'll start by sharing my screen — let me know if the deck pops up or the console.
[00:44] [screen share noise]
[00:47] Priya: ok, so this is the Redwood Console, top nav you see "Tracing", "Request Logs", "Models", "Rollouts". we'll click Tracing first.
[00:57] Tom: quick question — does tracing need any special agent on our side, or is it all server-side?
[01:02] Priya: good question. tracing is server-side for hosted and dedicated — we emit OpenTelemetry-style traces. for private on-prem we provide a lightweight collector config you can drop into your infra. no heavy agents required.
[01:14] Sara: and data residency — traces contain request metadata, do you mask prompt text by default?
[01:20] Priya: by default we do not store full prompt text in traces; there's a config for redaction and we can optionally mask tokens or store only hash/pseudonymized IDs. we'll share the security pack with exact defaults.
[01:31] Jordan: i'll drop the SOC2 and encryption docs in the follow-up.
[01:34] Maya: thanks.
[01:36] Priya: ok back to tracing — here's the trace list, you can filter by model, route, latency percentile, status code. you can click into a trace and it surfaces spans: routing, model-inference, kv-cache-hit, network call to external retriever, etc.
[01:52] [knocking sound on mic]
[01:54] Liam: sorry, laptop mic is a little noisy, i'll mute.
[01:56] Priya: no worries. so here's a typical span where inference took 1.2s, you can expand details to see host, GPU type, quantization profile, and the selected kernel. sometimes the transcription or console shows 'kv cash' instead of kv cache — we get that in logs too, minor OCR, haha.
[02:16] Maya: nice — can we tie a trace to the raw HTTP request body in request-logs? that's the main ask.
[02:22] Priya: yes — we generate a request_id for every incoming call and surface it in both the trace and the request-logs table. clicking the request-id opens the raw payload (or masked payload depending on your retention settings) and the corresponding trace view. i'll show that now.
[02:36] Priya: switching to Request Logs, here's a table of recent requests. filters on status, model, route, and a free-text search. if you click a row you get headers, payload (again masked per policy), response, latency, and the trace link.
[02:50] Ethan: are logs stored in our VPC for private deployment? we can't have logs going to a third-party storage for compliance reasons.
[02:58] Priya: for Private deployments logs can be stored in-customer VPC or on-prem object store. for Dedicated we provide options: encrypted S3 buckets in customer account or managed bucket with strict access controls.
[03:11] Sara: do you support KMS integration? we need HSM-backed keys for encryption-at-rest.
[03:16] Jordan: yes we support customer-managed KMS, and for some enterprise customers HSM integrations via our private offering.
[03:22] Maya: cool.
[03:24] Priya: ok now i'll demo an error scenario — we have an example trace for an increased 5xx rate coming from a batch of requests to a reranking route.
[03:33] [pause while navigating]
[03:35] Priya: here's a 5xx trace — top level shows a model error span and an upstream network call to our retriever. you can see an annotation that the model process ran out of memory during a long context window.
[03:47] Tom: do you capture GPU memory metrics per span?
[03:51] Priya: yes we include host-level metrics (GPU mem, GPU util, CPU, RSS) as span attributes for model-inference spans. that lets you correlate OOM events with concurrent batch size.
[04:02] Maya: i'm curious how you recommend debugging OOM vs tokenization issues — sometimes it's just an off-by-one in prompt concat.
[04:09] Priya: yep. first step is to click the request-row and inspect the payload (masked) to check sequence length, then look at batching attributes. we also surface the batch composition: whether this request was in a continuous batch and what other requests were coalesced. that helps detect batch-induced OOMs.
[04:24] Ethan: can we replay a single request against a pinned model version from the UI?
[04:29] Priya: we have a "Replay" button that re-submits the captured payload to a selected model/version in a sandbox environment — good for deterministic repros. note: payloads with PII are masked and the replay requires an explicit permission.
[04:44] Sara: what about retention, audit logs — we need a 12 month audit trail for regulatory reasons.
[04:49] Jordan: audit logs are separate from request logs — we can retain audit at 12 months, request logs retention is configurable per plan. for long-term retention we can push logs to customer's S3.
[04:59] Maya: ok do you have SLA around trace availability? we want the traces to be near real-time for on-call.
[05:05] Priya: traces are ingested and available within 2-5s in dedicated and hosted, usually under 3s. for private it depends on collector config and network, but we provide a local ingest mode for lower latency.
[05:18] Tom: let's walk through a debugging flow end-to-end — show us a spike, how you'd find root cause, and what remediation you'd try.
[05:25] Priya: sure — i'll pick a latency spike window from the Trace Dashboard. here's a cluster of high-p95 traces. clicking a sample trace shows a long network call to the retriever — looks like a downstream vector DB timed out and caused retries. you can expand the timeline and see repeated external-call spans.
[05:44] Ethan: that matches our monitoring where the retriever was 503ing for a few minutes last week. how do we set an automated alert for that?
[05:50] Priya: Console supports alerting targets — you can set alerts on error-rate by route, or on trace-level anomalies (e.g., sudden increase in external-span durations). alerts can integrate with PagerDuty/Slack.
[05:59] Jordan: we'll propose an alert policy template for Nebula as part of the POC.
[06:04] Maya: one more— around cost, if we reduce batch sizes to avoid OOMs, what's the impact to cost? any tooling in Optimize to suggest settings?
[06:12] Priya: yes Redwood Optimize gives recommendations — it analyzes latency distribution and suggests batching policies, kv-cache TTLs, and quantization profiles to reduce cost while meeting latency SLOs. we'll include Optimize suggestions in the POC report.
[06:26] [short silence while Priya pulls up the Optimize tab]
[06:31] Priya: here is a sample Optimize run — it recommended reducing max batch from 64 to 32 for that rerank route, enabling prefix caching on the retriever path, and using int8 quantization for the candidate-scoring model. estimated cost reduction about 28% with minimal p95 impact.
[06:48] Maya: that's promising. can you run the Optimize analysis on our historical traces if we provide them?
[06:54] Priya: yes, if you share sample request-logs we can run an offline analysis and return recommendations. that's part of the POC scope.
[07:02] Ethan: for the POC, how do we route traffic? do we need to mirror traffic to Redwood or run in-line?
[07:08] Jordan: two options — traffic mirror to Redwood endpoints for non-prod testing, or a staged rollout via a router that sends X% of production to Dedicated instance. we'll propose a safe plan.
[07:18] Sara: any chance of data exfiltration during replay or replaying masked payloads — we need to ensure replays don't leak to third party retrievers.
[07:25] Priya: replays happen in your sandbox environment and follow rollout policies; we can disable external retrievers during replay or route them back to your internal retriever endpoints in the VPC. replay requires explicit RBAC permission.
[07:36] Tom: do you support SSO and per-route RBAC? some of our internal users should only see traces for test routes.
[07:43] Jordan: yes SAML/SSO and granular RBAC are supported. we map roles to console permissions (view traces, replay, download request logs).
[07:50] Maya: perfect.
[07:52] Priya: ok final demo: i'll simulate a failing batch — notice here the trace shows a sudden increase in batch size from 16 to 96 due to a routing bug, leading to OOM on the model host. open the batch composition panel — you can see which request-ids were coalesced.
[08:08] [keyboard clack]
[08:10] Priya: from there, we can drill into the exact requests and replay a single request against a pinned model, or re-run the entire batch in a sandbox to reproduce the OOM. also you can set automatic fallback policy to a smaller model variant if OOMs exceed threshold.
[08:26] Ethan: fallback sounds useful — is that per-route?
[08:29] Priya: yes per-route and per-customer policy. you can define canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks in Rollouts.
[08:36] Maya: what about request-log export formats — parquet? JSONL? we need an efficient pipeline into our data lake.
[08:42] Priya: we support JSONL, Parquet, and direct push to customer S3 with partitioning by date and model.
[08:50] Jordan: ok quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/security pack, run a scoped Optimize + tracing analysis on Nebula's sample logs, and propose pilot pricing for a month of Dedicated throughput to mimic production traffic.
[09:04] Maya: that aligns with our plan. thanks.
[09:08] Jordan: any final questions?
[09:10] Sara: just confirm — is there a way to redact prompt tokens after the fact if we discover PII in logs?
[09:15] Priya: yes we have a retrospective redaction tool — you can request reprocessing of stored logs to mask or remove fields. that requires proper access controls.
[09:24] Tom: sounds good. we'll share samples by Friday.
[09:27] Jordan: great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a draft SOW.
[09:31] Maya: thanks all.
[09:33] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription occasionally mis-heard 'KV cache' as 'KV cash' and speaker labels were sometimes overlapping; overall medium quality.
